title: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria
subtitle: Acquired PIGA-mutant clone · hemolysis, thrombosis, marrow failure · diagnose by granulocyte FLAER flow, treat hemolysis or thrombosis with complement inhibition, vaccinate before starting
source: Compiled from ICCS/ESCCA flow guidance · IPIG · FDA labels · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, October 2026.

blocks.heading: Pathophysiology
items: Somatic PIGA mutation in a stem cell → no GPI anchor → CD55 + CD59 absent from every progeny cell → RBCs lysed by the alternative complement pathway. The clone expands only where the normal marrow is under immune attack — hence the overlap with aplastic anemia

Triad: intravascular hemolysis, thrombosis, marrow failure. Free Hb scavenges NO → dysphagia, abdominal pain, erectile dysfunction, pulmonary hypertension, CKD. Dark morning urine is the name, not the rule
Untreated natural history: median survival 10 yr; 39% had venous thrombosis Hillmen NEJM 1995, n=80. On eculizumab, survival matches age-matched controls Kelly Blood 2011

blocks.heading: Clinical features
items: DAT-negative intravascular hemolysis — high LDH, absent haptoglobin, hemoglobinuria or hemosiderinuria
Unexplained thrombosis at an unusual site — Budd-Chiari, mesenteric/portal, cerebral venous sinus, dermal — or thrombosis + hemolysis or cytopenias
Unexplained cytopenias — PNH is a marrow failure disorder: anemia with a retic low for the degree of hemolysis, or any cytopenia + hemolysis/thrombosis
Aplastic anemia: at diagnosis and periodically (yearly, or with any sign of hemolysis); hypoplastic MDS
Do not use Ham or sucrose lysis — obsolete. Do not send RBC CD55/CD59 alone

blocks.heading: Flow cytometry — ICCS/ESCCA
rows: FLAER + CD24, gated on CD15. The clone-size number — unaffected by hemolysis or transfusion
FLAER + CD14, gated on CD64. Confirms a second lineage
CD59, gated on CD235a. Type III = absent (lyses), type II = partial, type I = normal. Underestimates the clone — PNH RBCs are destroyed and transfused cells dilute
Routine ~1%. High-sensitivity 0.01% — needed for AA/MDS screening Borowitz 2010; Illingworth 2018
blocks.footnote: FLAER binds the GPI anchor itself, so it is lineage-agnostic — but it does not work on RBCs. Report % granulocyte, % monocyte and RBC type II + III separately.

blocks.heading: Monitoring
items: Each visit: CBC, retic, LDH, bili; DAT (C3) if anemic on a C5i; ferritin, B12, folate periodically
Flow clone size every 6–12 mo (granulocytes) — and in AA/MDS patients without PNH, yearly screening
Renal function; new cytopenias → marrow (AA or MDS evolution)

boxes: urgent start: antibiotic cover until 2 wk post-vaccine
C5i: ravulizumab IV q8wk or crovalimab SC q4wk
Hb, LDH, retic, bili, transfusions, DAT (C3)

chains.header: On a C5 inhibitor and still anemic
boxes: LDH ≤1.5× ULN + high retic + DAT C3+ → EVH
low retic → marrow failure, iron, B12, folate
or allo-HCT; complement Rx only for hemolysis
severe aplastic anemia / MDS or AML evolution
despite inhibition, or no access to inhibitors

blocks.heading: Who needs treatment
items: Treat: symptomatic hemolysis (transfusion need, fatigue, smooth-muscle symptoms), any thrombosis, hemolysis-related organ damage (renal, pulmonary hypertension), pregnancy
Watch: subclinical or small clones without hemolysis — CBC + LDH, repeat flow every 6–12 mo

blocks.heading: Baseline labs
items: Hemolysis: LDH (the IVH marker), retic, haptoglobin, indirect bili, free Hb, UA + urine hemosiderin. DAT negative (becomes C3d+ on a C5 inhibitor)
Iron, B12, folate: chronic hemoglobinuria causes iron deficiency; on C5i, transfused EVH can swing to overload
CBC + marrow biopsy with cytogenetics if any cytopenia — is there AA or MDS underneath? Creatinine; imaging only for symptoms

blocks.heading: IPIG classification — Parker 2005
rows: Clinical IVH, cellular marrow, no other marrow disorder. Usually a large clone
Hemolysis with AA or low-risk MDS documented — treat whichever dominates
Small clone, no clinical or lab hemolysis; seen in AA/MDS. No complement therapy — monitor the clone

blocks.heading: Thrombosis
items: Leading cause of death in PNH. Mostly venous, often unusual sites; can occur on therapeutic anticoagulation
Clone size predicts it: granulocyte clone >50% → 10-yr risk 44% vs 5.8% Hall Blood 2003

Acute event: therapeutic LMWH/UFH + start complement inhibition now — anticoagulation alone does not stop it. Eculizumab cut events 7.37 → 1.07/100 pt-yr Hillmen Blood 2007. Continue anticoagulation long term after a thrombosis

Primary prophylaxis: not routine on a complement inhibitor — 21 patients without prior thrombosis stopped warfarin with no events Kelly 2011. Warfarin for clone >50% Hall 2003 is the no-access fallback

blocks.heading: AA / PNH overlap
items: Small PNH clones are common in AA — screen by high-sensitivity flow; a clone supports immune-mediated AA
Clones can expand after IST into hemolytic PNH (or vanish) — re-check flow at least yearly
Severe marrow failure is treated as AA (IST or transplant); complement inhibition only for clinically significant hemolysis

Clone size — rough guide, no cutoff defines PNH (category = hemolysis + marrow status): <10% usually subclinical (typical in AA) · 10–50% grey zone, check LDH/retic/haptoglobin · >50% typical of classic PNH, highest thrombosis risk

blocks.heading: Infection safety
items: MenACWY + MenB ≥2 wk before the first dose; if treatment cannot wait, give antibiotic prophylaxis until 2 wk after vaccination. Revaccinate per ACIP for as long as the patient is on therapy
Proximal inhibitors (pegcetacoplan, iptacopan, danicopan) also block opsonization → boxed warning extends to S. pneumoniae and Hib; vaccinate against pneumococcus (Hib per ACIP)
Vaccines do not fully protect — meningococcal disease has occurred in vaccinated patients. Every patient carries the safety card
Fever or meningism = emergency: blood cultures + empiric ceftriaxone immediately, then evaluate

blocks.heading: Pregnancy
items: High-risk for thrombosis, peaking postpartum. Use eculizumab or ravulizumab; proximal agents lack human data — switch before conception
Eculizumab, 75 pregnancies: no maternal deaths, 3 fetal deaths (4%); dose/frequency increased in 54%; LMWH in 88%; both thromboses postpartum Kelly NEJM 2015
Prophylactic LMWH through pregnancy and the postpartum period; expect to escalate the C5i in the 2nd–3rd trimester

blocks.heading: Agents — dosing
rows: C5, IV. 600 mg weekly ×4 → 900 mg wk 5 → 900 mg q2wk
q2wk infusions; trough BTH. C5 R885H variant: no response
C5, IV, weight-based load → maintenance 2 wk later, then q8wk: 40–<60 kg 2400 → 3000 mg · 60–<100 kg 2700 → 3300 · ≥100 kg 3000 → 3600. Switching: load 2 wk after last eculizumab
C5 (different epitope). D1 1000 mg IV (1500 if ≥100 kg) → 340 mg SC D2, 8, 15, 22 → 680 mg SC q4wk from D29 (1020 if ≥100 kg). Switching: load at the next scheduled dose
Switch from ecu/ravu → type III immune-complex reactions (19% per label). Works in R885H
C3, SC. 1080 mg twice weekly; every 3 d if LDH >2× ULN. From eculizumab: overlap 4 wk, then stop it; from ravulizumab: start ≤4 wk after last dose
Factor B, oral. 200 mg BID. Start ≤1 wk after last eculizumab or ≤6 wk after last ravulizumab
Missed doses → hemolysis. Monitor ≥2 wk after stopping
Factor D, oral, added to ravulizumab/eculizumab. 150 mg TID → 200 mg TID if Hb rise <2 g/dL at 4 wk or transfused
blocks.footnote: All six carry a boxed warning for serious meningococcal infection and are REMS-restricted. No approval yet for pozelimab + cemdisiran (investigational).

blocks.heading: Breakthrough hemolysis (BTH)
items: BTH = return of IVH on therapy: LDH up, dark urine, Hb falls, symptoms back
Pharmacokinetic (C5i): drug runs out before the next dose — classic late in the eculizumab interval. Fix: shorten the interval / raise the dose, or move to ravulizumab 301: BTH 4.0% vs 10.7%
Pharmacodynamic: a complement-amplifying trigger — infection, surgery, pregnancy, vaccination. Treat the trigger; give an extra C5i dose

On a proximal inhibitor BTH can be abrupt and severe — the whole, now-unprotected PNH RBC mass lyses at once. Check adherence, give a C5i rescue dose (eculizumab/ravulizumab), transfuse, involve a PNH center
Never stop a proximal inhibitor abruptly — rebound hemolysis; bridge directly to another agent

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: Eculizumab vs placebo, transfused pts (n=87): Hb stabilized 49% vs 0%; median 0 vs 10 units
Single-arm, broader population (n=97): LDH ↓87%; 51% transfusion-free for 52 wk
Ravulizumab q8wk noninferior to eculizumab q2wk in naive (n=246) and switched (n=195) patients
Crovalimab vs eculizumab, naive (n=204): hemolysis control 79.3% vs 79.0%, noninferior. COMMODORE 3 (China, single-arm) supportive
Switch from eculizumab, Hb <10.5 (n=80): pegcetacoplan Hb +3.84 g/dL vs eculizumab; transfusion-free 85% vs 15%
Naive, vs supportive care (n=53): Hb stabilization 85.7% vs 0%
Anti-C5 with Hb <10 → switch to iptacopan (n=97): Hb ↑≥2 g/dL in 51/60 vs 0/35; Hb ≥12 in 42/60
Naive, single-arm (n=40): Hb ↑≥2 g/dL in 31/33; no transfusions
Danicopan added to C5i for cs-EVH: Hb +2.94 vs +0.50 g/dL at 12 wk (diff 2.44)

blocks.heading: Pearls
items: On a C5i the RBC clone grows — PNH RBCs now survive. That is treatment effect, not progression; follow the granulocyte clone
DAT C3d+ on a C5i = EVH, not a new autoimmune hemolysis
LDH on a C5i usually sits ≤1.5× ULN; a sudden rise is BTH until proven otherwise
C5 R885H polymorphism (described in Japanese patients): no response to eculizumab or ravulizumab — crovalimab binds a different C5 epitope
Eculizumab/ravulizumab protect against thrombosis, but after a thrombosis anticoagulation continues
